events.title: US midterm general election, 3 November 2026

scope.appliesTo: Federal, state and local offices and ballot measures

events.outcome: Results partly preliminary at capture. TIME reports Democrats won control of Congress; an NBC exit poll found 56% of voters called AI and data centers a crucial or major factor.
uncertaintyNotes: Many contests were uncalled at capture
An election outcome enacts no data-center rule

events.title: Ohio US Senate: Sherrod Brown reported winner over Jon Husted
events.outcome: Brown reported to have won by about five points after ads calling Husted "the face of data centers in Ohio". Brown's own policy position is not stated in the source.
uncertaintyNotes: Call status not stated by the source
A Senate seat confers no state or local permitting power

events.title: Kansas governor: Cindy Holscher leading; campaign called for a data-center pause

scope.appliesTo: Campaign pledge for a pause until guardrails are set

uncertaintyNotes: A campaign pledge is not a proposal, bill or rule

events.title: New York Executive Order 62: DEC permit applications for ≥50 MW data centers held in abeyance
events.expiryCondition: Until DPS submits the final Generic Environmental Impact Statement and findings statement; no fixed end date

scope.appliesTo: DEC discretionary permits, approvals and licences to build or expand facilities consuming or able to consume ≥50 MW, for applications not deemed complete before the order
scope.exemptions: Local-government permits; facilities primarily used for manufacturing, research, education or medical care; applications deemed complete before the order

events.outcome: Executive action in force; DEC water-withdrawal review report due within twelve months.
uncertaintyNotes: Termination depends on GEIS completion, not a date
Applicability to a specific project requires DEC completeness records, which were not retrieved
The order text states no separate effective date; the signing date is used

events.title: New York Responsible Data Center Development Act (S10642 / A11560): passed legislature, not shown as signed
events.expiryCondition: One year after the effective date, if enacted

scope.appliesTo: DEC permits, certificates, registrations or licences for large data centers (peak demand ≥20 MW)
scope.exemptions: Modifications or renewals of existing approvals; facilities that began construction on or before the effective date

events.outcome: Senate passed A11560 on 4 June 2026 (43–17). The bill page shows no delivery, signature, veto or chapter number at capture.
uncertaintyNotes: Secondary coverage reports conflicting status, including one claim of signature that the legislative record does not show
Not enacted: the governor acted through EO 62 instead

events.title: Oklahoma HB 2992, Data Center Consumer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026

scope.appliesTo: New large-load users of ≥75 MW (data centers, AI computing, cryptocurrency mining) bear their own energy-infrastructure costs; developers notify nearby landowners, county commissioners and the Corporation Commission within 60 days of acquiring land

events.outcome: Signed by Governor Stitt (date not stated in the official release); effective 1 July 2026.
uncertaintyNotes: Enrolled bill text and exact signing date not retrieved
Cost-allocation detail depends on Corporation Commission implementation

events.title: Arizona budget: three-year pause on new data-center transaction-privilege tax exemption applications
events.expiryCondition: Reported to run through 2029 unless incentives are eliminated

scope.appliesTo: New applications to the Arizona Commerce Authority for data-center TPT and use-tax exemptions
scope.exemptions: Applications filed before the end of June 2026 (treatment of existing certifications not stated)

events.outcome: Applications closed at the end of June 2026; many operators filed before the deadline.
uncertaintyNotes: Bill number, signing date and exact end date not identified

events.title: US District Court (S.D. Ohio): Wilmington must redo three ordinances before deciding the Amazon site plan
events.expiryCondition: Until the generator-noise, rezoning and permitted-use ordinances are redone with required notice

scope.appliesTo: Decision on the Amazon data center site plan; public comment at planning commission

events.outcome: The city cannot decide the site plan until it redoes the ordinances; the case continues in federal court.
uncertaintyNotes: Whether the September re-enactment satisfied the order is not established by the retrieved sources
Court order not retrieved directly; reported by WYSO

events.title: Wilmington emergency rezoning of the 471-acre Cosler Farm parcel to light industrial

scope.appliesTo: Permits data center construction in a light-industrial zone on the parcel proposed for the Amazon campus

events.outcome: Emergency ordinances take effect immediately and cannot be referred; a resident sued in Clinton County Common Pleas Court. The city agreed not to act for one week pending a TRO hearing.

events.title: Wilmington referenda: four rezonings (≈545 acres near US 68 / SR 730) rejected

scope.appliesTo: February 2026 rezonings of four parcels from rural residential to light industrial (65.29, 191.12, 119.373 and 170.11 acres)

events.outcome: Voters rejected the rezoning ordinances by about 80% to 20% (final unofficial).
uncertaintyNotes: Parcels are adjacent to, and "could be related" to, the Amazon campus; they are not the 471-acre Cosler parcel

events.title: Piqua charter amendment banning data centers

scope.appliesTo: WYSO: data centers above 25 MW of peak demand; tracker: ban on construction

events.outcome: Approved (tracker: 67% to 33%); final unofficial. City: "unclear at this time if and how" it affects the Meta project underway.
uncertaintyNotes: Sources differ on scope (25 MW threshold vs outright construction ban)
Applicability to the existing Meta project undetermined by the city

events.title: Urbana charter amendment banning large data centers

scope.appliesTo: WYSO: data centers above 7.5 MW of peak demand; tracker: ban within city limits

events.outcome: Approved (tracker: 77% to 23%); effect on Thor Equities' proposed Urbana Technology Hub unclear given a state appeal and federal lawsuit.

events.title: Janesville referendum: voter approval required for GM/JATCO site projects over $450 million

scope.appliesTo: Development agreements, projects, sales or leases at the former GM/JATCO site above $450 million total cost

uncertaintyNotes: The question does not name data centers

events.title: Harwood initiative for added review before approving industrial development

scope.appliesTo: Additional review before approving industrial development

events.outcome: Defeated (tracker: 25% yes / 75% no). Rejection adds no new review requirement.
